title: Jacket potatoes with split pea dal and spring greens

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain tin and dried pulse, with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Baking potatoes, yellow split peas, tinned tomatoes, spring greens and the spices are everyday Tesco items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking tray and one large pan, using simple baking and simmering.

works.reason: 200g split peas in 900ml water with a tin of tomatoes simmered for 50 minutes gives a thick dal that suits four jacket potatoes, and the spices, salt and lemon season it properly.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers chopping an onion and garlic, shredding greens and prepping potatoes, and the 75-minute cook matches the 1¼-hour bake, with the dal fitting inside it.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, the names match their ids, and only water is added unlisted.

seasonal_feel.reason: 300g of spring greens wilted through a warming dal on a jacket potato is a substantial part of the dish and right for a cool mid-March lunch.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potatoes, pulses and a good portion of greens make a filling, wholesome meal a family would happily eat again.
